ct_basin_area.blurb: Basin Area is the bouldering heart of Bald Rock Basin, in the Danbury area of western Connecticut near Redding and Bethel. A drainage basin falls away to the west below the power lines, and outcrops and boulders run along its ridge edge down to the floor. The boulders are large gneiss. Everything here is a boulder problem, from V-easy through V9, with the bulk between V0 and V5 and a few harder ones. East Side has the most problems, with El Duque Wall and Vernal Cave; West Side holds the King, Colossus and Warmup boulders; South Side is the smallest of the three.

id_mortal_earth.blurb: Mortal Earth is a sport-only section of the Fins, in Central Idaho at the southern end of the Lost River Range. The rock is grey limestone, vertical to a little less than vertical with the odd small roof, and chert supplies positive holds of every size. Expect pockets, pinches, rails, crimps and runnels, and technical, sustained climbing that is generally less steep than the main Fins. Grades run from about 5.6 to the middle of 5.12, with the large majority at 5.10 and 5.11. Climbs are mostly one or two pitches. Psychedelic Rock, Cannonball Wall, Classic Rock and Wonderwall are among its 17 crags. For the Fins as a whole, walls get morning sun and are mostly in full shade by 1 pm.

nv_reno_bouldering.blurb: Reno Bouldering gathers scattered boulder spots in and around Reno, in western Nevada, and every climb is a boulder problem. The grades skew easy: V0 and V1 are the most common, thinning steadily through V4 with a few V5 to V7. Somersett Boulders is the largest piece. There the middle zone has sharp, tan granite boulders, while the Primordial Soup zone to the north is steep and overhanging on friable sandstone. Evans Canyon, Galena/Freeway Boulders and Upper Keystone Canyon are the other bigger groups.

on_the_bluffs.blurb: The Bluffs is a climbing park inside the city of Thunder Bay, just north of downtown. The cliff line runs for more than a kilometre. The cliffs are known for crack climbing. Trad and top-rope lines dominate, with a few aid, sport and boulder problems. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.12, with many moderates between 5.5 and 5.10. Powerline Corridor holds the most routes, followed by Land of Many Uses, Split Beaver and Orangeman Wall.

va_cascades_bouldering.blurb: Cascades Bouldering is in the Cascades Recreation Area near Pembroke in southwest Virginia, about half an hour from Blacksburg and Virginia Tech. Nearly all of it is bouldering on mostly sandstone, with slopers, pinches and a few small crimps, and a mix of slabs, vertical faces, roofs and steeper lines, some boulders sitting by the stream. Friction is especially good in cooler months. Grades climb from V0 through the mid-range, with the heaviest concentration from V2 to V6 and a few V8 to V10 problems. Cascadia Area has the most climbs, with its streamside roofed boulder; Pyramid Area is a boulderfield with slab lines, followed by Title Fight and Contrast.
